source.section: PDF page 10, Line 29, Married taxpayers (each spouse up to 20,000 of own income; no unused part of the spouse's exclusion; example 30,000 and 15,000 gives 35,000); Form IT-201 line 29; Form IT-201 lines 19, 24, 32-39 (PDF pages 2-3); IT-201-I PDF page 11 (line 34 standard deduction table), PDF pages 12 and 33 (line 39, rate schedule)

worked: Married filing jointly, both 62 (59 1/2 before 2025). Person 0: private employer pension 30,000. Person 1: 401(k) periodic distributions 15,000 and wages 75,000. The booklet's example: 20,000 + 15,000 = 35,000. Federal AGI (IT-201 line 19) = 120,000.00. Federal taxable income = 120,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 88,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtraction: line 29 exclusion, person 0: private pension 30,000, limited to 20,000 20,000.00. Subtraction: line 29 exclusion, person 1: 401(k) periodic distribution 15,000 (person 0's unused amount cannot be used) 15,000.00. Line 32 total subtractions = 35,000.00. Line 33 New York AGI = 120,000.00 - 35,000.00 = 85,000.00. Line 34 New York standard deduction (married joint, PDF page 11 table) 16,050.00; line 35 = 85,000.00 - 16,050.00 = 68,950.00; line 36 dependent exemption 0 (no dependents); lines 37/38 taxable income 68,950.00. Rate schedule (PDF page 33, married joint) on 68,950.00: 17,150.00 x 4% = 686.00; 6,450.00 x 4.5% = 290.25; 4,300.00 x 5.25% = 225.75; 41,050.00 x 5.5% = 2,257.75; schedule tax = 3,459.75. NY AGI is 107,650 or less and line 38 is 65,000 or more: the rate schedule applies (PDF page 12, line 39); no recapture worksheet. Line 39 NYS tax = 3,459.75. Credits: none (the household credit, line 40, PDF page 12 tables 1-3, allows no credit above federal AGI of 28,000 single or 32,000 other statuses): state income tax = 3,459.75.
